summary: Founding sweep. It started from five sources the reader supplied, then ran three searches for what they left out. The same day the reader clarified that local means fitted to what you have, so the on-device claim was retired, and asked for a complete list of who is building the loop, which a second check extended. 37 signals are active.

changes.text: The reader is tracking this as a provider. Added what the evidence implies for a provider, flagged the three claims that position rests on (C4, C7, C3), and opened three provider-side checks (W12 to W14).
The reader clarified that local means fitted to what you have (different devices), not on-device hardware. The framing is restated in those terms and that part now holds.

A roster of every team found that has described the loop: 25 entries with a one-line gist each. A second check found five not seen before (RoofLang, an NPU kernel loop, KDA, FlashVector, Astra); five the first sweep saw and left out are now listed too. Two became signals.
Widened from the workload to what you have: traffic, model and chip together. Confidence unchanged at 0.8.
The on-device claim is retired as out of scope, with five signals that only argued for or against local hardware. Four that show per-device specialisation now count under C2.
Dropped. It was premised on the on-device reading.
W4 and W9 dropped as out of scope. W11 opened: one system showing different winners on two chip families.
Eight claims opened, C1 to C8, each with a starting confidence and named conditions for moving it.
The reader's framing judged for the first time. Workload-aware holds. Local and RSI do not, in the senses those words usually carry.
40 signals: 7 read first-hand, 33 relayed by research sub-agents and marked as such. Relayed ones should be opened and confirmed over the next few sweeps, most load-bearing first.
Six tensions opened. The megakernel split (T1) is the most concrete: two camps shipped opposite bets in the same month.
Ten dated checks opened. The first due is confirming the canonical AgentX scoreboard and recording today's top results as a baseline.
Vocabulary fixed: eight stack layers, five ways an optimisation gets produced, five venues, four timescales, five loop stages.
inference-rsi.com resolved: it is the project page for Evolving Infra (MIT HAN Lab and others, arXiv 2611.12304). Despite the domain, neither page nor paper claims self-improvement.

swept: The five reader-supplied sources and the pages they cite
Agent-driven and self-improving inference optimisation, February to November 2026, including critiques and failed replications
Workload-aware and per-customer serving across providers, open engines and papers
Local runtimes, ML compilers and kernel generation, plus essays for and against local inference
A second check for loop announcements missed: other providers, chip vendors, model labs and the public scoreboard
